_comment: Cross-client name order (T-176): lists on the overview, categories, items, the All items
screen. ONE file, read by BOTH test suites, like expense-arithmetic.json: web/src/lib/
nameOrder.test.ts imports it and Android's NameOrderTest reads it from the repo root.
The sort key of a name: NFKD-decompose it, drop every combining mark (so accents go), lowercase
it without a locale, fold the few letters that do not decompose (ß ss, æ ae, œ oe, ø o, đ d,
ł l, þ th), then drop anything before the first letter or digit — emoji, symbols, spaces.
Keys compare by UTF-16 code unit, as both JavaScript and Kotlin compare strings. Equal keys
fall back to the full name, the same way, and then to the id, so the order is total.
Deliberately not a platform collator: Intl.Collator and java.text.Collator disagree in
details, and the point of this is that both clients agree exactly. Digits are not read as
numbers: '10 things' sorts before '2 things'. Kana voicing marks decompose into combining
marks too, so ご sorts with こ, which is also how a Japanese dictionary orders them.

orders.name: accents, case and a leading emoji do not move a name out of its letter
equal keys fall back to the full name, then the id
a name with no letters or digits sorts first
Cyrillic sorts within itself, ё with е
